Our itinerary includes two additional days for the summit attempt, providing greater opportunities to reach the top in case of adverse weather conditions or acclimatization needs.

NOTE: The proposed itinerary is subject to changes due to weather conditions or force majeure that may endanger the group’s safety. The guides reserve the authority to modify the program at their discretion. You can be sure that any change will have two fundamental objectives: maximizing safety and the chances of success, based on the knowledge and experience of our guides.

blocks.text:
## Expedition to the highest peak in South America

You spend the first few days in Mendoza and on the approach to Aconcagua. From there, you gain altitude in stages via Confluencia and Plaza de Mulas. Before the summit attempt, the itinerary includes acclimatisation outings to Plaza Francia, Mount Bonete and the high camps.

## Carrying equipment between high camps

The expedition includes porter support so you can save your energy for the climb.

There is one porter for every three participants. Each porter can carry up to 20 kg on each leg.

Porters carry shared expedition equipment, including tents and cooking gear, on the following legs:

1. Confluencia to Plaza de Mulas
2. Plaza de Mulas to Plaza Canadá
3. Plaza Canadá to Nido de Cóndores
4. Nido de Cóndores to Berlín–Cólera
5. Berlín–Cólera to Plaza de Mulas on the descent

You carry your own sleeping bag, clothing, summit pack, mountaineering boots and other personal equipment.

You can hire a separate porter for your personal gear at an additional cost.

## Guides

Qualified mountain guides from the Argentine Mountain Guides Association (AAGM) or the Mendoza Mountain Guide School (EPGAMT) accompany the expedition.

There is one guide for every three participants.

The guides carry a VHF radio, a first-aid kit, altitude sickness medication, ropes, an altimeter, a digital pulse oximeter and the necessary mountaineering equipment.

## Reserve days and itinerary changes

Reserve days are used only when circumstances prevent the expedition from following its planned itinerary.

The guides may change the itinerary if the weather, route conditions or group safety require it. Itinerary changes in these circumstances do not qualify for financial compensation.

## Tents

At the high camps, we use quality mountaineering tents, including the North Face VE 25 and Mountain Hardwear Trango 3.1.

A tent usually sleeps two people.

The weather on Aconcagua can change quickly, even in summer, so reliable tents are an important part of expedition safety.

## Communications

The expedition uses fixed and portable communications equipment.

VHF and SSB (BLU) radio links connect the high camps, Plaza de Mulas, Confluencia, Puente del Inca and Mendoza.

A satellite phone is also available.

## Certificate

After the expedition, you receive a certificate signed by the guide and the managing director of Acomara-AconcaguaExpeditions.com.

It confirms your participation and, if you reach the summit, records your ascent of Aconcagua.

## Medical assistance after the expedition

If you are evacuated from the mountain or feel unwell after returning, our support team can help arrange medical care in Mendoza.

If needed, the team can help arrange further examinations, obtain medication or organise hospital treatment.

Doctors' fees, examinations and medication are excluded from the price.

## Support in Mendoza

After the expedition, our support team can help you change or buy tickets, return rented equipment, store luggage and find general information.
